answer: Mid-slope fruit rows issue a single terrace berth to one picker. She bonds 23.1 POA in the shed till, must seat a stamped marble weight in the berth cup before the 06:20 drip bell, and after the first 16-minute thinning she draws a wet chalk tick across the weight serial that the row clerk photographs against the cup stamp on that vine. A second weight, a bell missed by more than 45 seconds, or a tick that skips two digits forfeits 11.2 POA and frees the berth; two faults in four mornings void the row claim.
